headline: JPMorgan Chase chief executive Jamie Dimon told AI companies to build data centres where local people want them instead of fighting opposition.
score_reason: Pool 5 lowered by 1: the interview was on 7 Oct and other outlets reported it on 8 Oct; Moneywise republished it on 10 Oct.
importance_line: A leading banker tells AI firms that public opposition is a fight they will not win, which matters first to people near planned data centres and those worried about power bills, then to local officials and AI companies; it is one executive's view from an interview on 7 Oct, and the community commitments he describes are not verified.
summary: Bloomberg News reports, as relayed by Moneywise, that JPMorgan Chase chief executive Jamie Dimon said in an interview on 7 Oct that AI companies should build data centres 'where they're wanted' because local opposition is a fight they are 'not going to win', and that many are already making commitments not to raise consumers' electricity costs. Moneywise adds that data centres are a political flashpoint before the November midterm elections, with a Pew Research Center poll published 22 Sep finding that 50 percent of Americans say they hurt home energy costs and 54 percent say they harm the environment; Dimon also said AI will 'cure a lot of diseases' but called the agent risks 'a legitimate concern'.
notes: Quotes come from Bloomberg News' 7 Oct interview, whose own link is not known; the text was read on Yahoo Finance's copy of the Moneywise article, and url is the Moneywise original (403 here). Old news re-dated: expect it to be held back as stale.
